record_notes.DCP-LETT-2060: Undated Darwin ALS, all eight retained blocks, excluded divided-to-save-postage note, full footnotes and bibliography read. P3–6 explicitly answer the tree-sex question with a qualified occasional-crossing hypothesis, acknowledged Leguminosae counterexamples and proposed nursery/Robinia enquiries; probability ratios are illustrative, not measurements. Macarthur report is oral. Bentham objection lacks a specifically identified surviving incoming text here. P7 first sentence thanks the protean list; the rest forwards Watson note/essay and distinguishes close species from variable species. Source 2063 supports the latter clarification; third-party 2065 separately cited but not yet admitted. Previous March 15 Gray knowledge retained. No Japanese-flora discussion falsely assigned to this response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2089: May 9, supplied 1857, twelve retained blocks, notes and bibliography read. New Statistics part already received and read; query about 49 species and 44 maximum genera is based on an error Gray later corrects. Explicitly asks tree-sex counts, following earlier theoretical letter. Introduced/native proportions based on older notes and first Manual edition are tentative, then called chance or errors; do not report universal agreement. Eight genuine MathML fractions in four paired British table rows verified: 1/10 versus 1/9, 1/22 versus 1/23, 1/28 versus 1/30, 1/20 versus 1/18. Earlier US Compositae string 18 has no fraction markup in raw HTML; retain ambiguity rather than silently substituting 1/8. record_notes.DCP-LETT-2104: Incomplete Gray ALS, nine retained blocks, annotations, notes and bibliography read. Approximately May 24, 1857 is conjectured from June 1 last-week dispatch and an ink June 9 docket, only probably a receipt date. No exact composition or definite June 9 arrival assigned. P1–6 answer Watson categories forwarded with Darwin March letter, not May 9 Statistics question. Close species versus variation depends on differing taxonomic circumscription: Boott/Hooker Carex, Tuckerman/Gray Potamogeton and uncertain Ranunculus identities. Gray calls earlier list rough, greater part variable with six explicit exclusions and a Solidago question mark. P7 asks criticism of last article already sent as sheets, P8 asks posting three enclosures; their texts absent. Missing beginning may have carried June 18 crossing remarks, but no text reconstructed. Chapter annotation is separate from incoming voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2109: June 18, supplied 1857, seven retained blocks, full notes and bibliography read. Thanks two Gray letters; missing corrected/duplicate Silliman copy is separate from article sheets previously read in May. P1 final sentence answers surviving Watson-category comments in 2104. P2–4 respond to June 1 disjoined-species, introduced-family and tree-sex information. P2 extinction is a tentative common-cause hypothesis, not a demonstrated universal distribution law. Raw P4 95132 has no MathML; 95/132 interpretation is supported by explicit June 1 counts, with raw text preserved. P5 crossing/bud remarks have no complete surviving incoming passage in either June 1 or the incomplete May letter and remain a missing-input section; named literature not itself a recovered prompt. Summary incorrectly suggests underwater Leguminosae; body distinguishes Podostemon/Subularia under water and parenthetical Leguminosæ. P7 measured 60-yard holly observation with 20 sampled stigmas is Darwin additional evidence, not Gray observation. At Moor Park despite printed Down address, not a second date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2120: July 7, 1857, eleven retained blocks, all annotations, notes and bibliography read. Explicitly acknowledges June 18 letter received last week. Last-week dispatch by private ship passenger to Liverpool of Watson papers, pamphlet and First Lessons is not Darwin receipt or reading. P3–7 accept extinction for some disjunctions while challenging universal contraction and continuous ancestral areas; Sarraceniaceae and Cladrastis examples remain questions, not proofs of original range. Gray says no theory prejudice but supplies qualified first-view objections. P8 crossing is a vera causa with uncertain extent and papilionaceous/Fumariaceae counterexamples. P9 explicitly retracts his untested grass-bud claim after fresh observations of named grasses around his door. P10 similarly qualifies Compositae inference, not a completed universal disproof; responds to holly observation. Darwin divided manuscript across chapter files later; annotations do not split authorship or composition dates.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2125: July 20, supplied 1857, seven retained blocks, full footnotes and bibliography read. Direct response to July 7 extinction objections and fertilization discussion. P1–2 explain nineteen-year inquiry and provisional transmutation hypothesis, common-descent rationale for shared area, substantial exceptions and Hooker reaction to distribution chapter; these are Darwin arguments with admitted difficulties, not settled independent creation or proof. Hooker never-so-shaky reaction matches 1983 P1 and is separately a later knowledge witness. P3 thanks corrected grass observations. P4 retains absence of demonstrated crossing of garden varieties while describing insect mechanics in kidney bean, Lathyrus and broom; marginal NB scratched left wing-petals repeats July 19 observation, distinct from future Gray inspection. P5 Our theory refers occasional cross-fertilization, not every statement of transmutation. P1–5 form coherent reply scope; final thanks/signature remain context.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2063: Additional incomplete Watson March 10, 1857 source fully read: five retained blocks, salutation, annotations, footnotes and bibliography. Defines three alternative meanings of variable genera with Carex/Ranunculus, Rubus/Hieracium and Viola/Saxifraga examples. Distinguishes close stable species from inseparable variable complexes. Thinks Gray may mean first while Darwin means second or third, but text ends mid-sentence after copy proposal; no missing continuation invented. Raw yes certainly has no separate-hand markup, so no attribution silently changed. Darwin Please return and 1) annotations separately support forwarded note identification; March 16–31 outgoing 2060 explicitly forwards numbered note and asks Gray about this precise distinction. Companion Watson-to-Gray essay 2065 awaits supplemental admission.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1982: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional Gray November 4, 1856 source, all twenty-five blocks including initial eight statistical rows, notes, annotations and bibliography read. visual_readings.visual_observation: Schematic America/Europe northern map, point p, White Mountains and Alps, curved isotherms labelled 40° and 50°, glacial-sea boundary and connecting island/land shapes. Temperature scale is not stated; these are isotherms, not observed latitude contours or a calibrated reconstructed map.

Unlabelled inclined section with a double sloping line, small intermediate rise and hatched cap at upper right, adjacent to humidity/elevation remarks. No numerical dimensions, scale or explicit directional legend; preserve as visual source rather than invent quantified geographic content.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
